# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

Every applicable rule is Clear, as read from code. Nothing in the code is unknown, but a CDN or firewall in front of the site could still change what crawlers receive. The code can't show that.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing in the code is broken. The one open question is outside the code.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers can get through your CDN or firewall
- **Why it matters:** The code allows search crawlers, but a CDN or firewall in front of the site could still block them, and code can't show that.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` followed by `Allow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** The code score stays 100–100. This check can't change it, because no rule is waiting on it. It settles the real-world question.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | `public/robots.txt`: plain text, valid lines, tiny file |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-3`: `*` is allowed, only `/account` is disallowed. Policy is `allow` for AI search. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 indexable routes have no noindex. `app/account/page.tsx:1` is noindex but isn't in the sitemap or the navigation. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on own origin | Clear | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: absolute URLs on `www.orchard.example` |
| GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Clear | Server Components in every page, with no client fetching |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found in any file |
| GEO-011 | Valid sitemap is discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid and `robots.txt:11` has an absolute `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. 3 of 3 indexable routes have a title and description. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable through links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:7`: plain `<a href>` links to all three pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions vs. AI-search policy | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0`. The `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:9` is a scoped choice. |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | I read all 5 files in `app/`. There are no images, the links have text, and every page has a title. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app profile declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | None present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not scored | None present |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Add a `<lastmod>` to each sitemap entry:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.orchard.example/</loc></url>`. Real update dates help crawlers decide what to re-read.
- **Label the business with structured data:** No JSON-LD exists. Organization (or LocalBusiness) data in `app/layout.tsx` could state the name, URL and location that `app/page.tsx:4` already shows ("Grown in Herefordshire since 1952").
- **Give the visit page the details it promises:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`. The page has only one sentence and no directions or address. Adding the address and the days and hours, then labelling them as LocalBusiness `openingHours`, would match the description.
- **Name the varieties:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` The page names two of the forty. A list, with a page per variety (for example `/varieties/ashmeads-kernel`), would back up the claim and give each variety its own address.
- **Link onward from the home page:** `app/page.tsx:4` has one sentence and no links beyond the navigation. Links from the intro to varieties and visiting would connect related pages.
- **Add a default title and description in the layout:** `app/layout.tsx:1` sets only `metadataBase`. A fallback would protect any page added later that forgets its own.
- **Add a description to the account page:** `app/account/page.tsx:1` has a title but no description. This is optional, because the page is deliberately noindexed.
- **Add the city or region to titles:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Visit the orchard'`. The title doesn't say whose orchard or where, which a title like "Visit Orchard, Herefordshire" would.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** Code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses, or give me the URL for a live check.
- **Live-only checks:** I read the real status codes, redirects, `X-Robots-Tag` headers and sitemap URL responses from code only. A live scan would confirm them, but they don't change the results above.
- **Training crawlers:** `public/robots.txt:5-9` blocks `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot`. That matches your `trainingCrawlers: "block"` policy and isn't counted.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find the site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- I read `package.json`, `geo.config.json`, the 5 files in `app/`, `public/robots.txt` and `public/sitemap.xml`. That is every tracked file, with 4 routes (3 indexable plus the account page). I found no JSON-LD sources, middleware or `next.config`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
